challenges.name: agent-budget-quiz
challenges.title: Before or after the call?
challenges.description: Two budget checks from the CodeDev tutor agent: one that adds up usage after each call, and one that estimates the next call before it runs.

questions.explanation: False. The check runs after the call, so it can only notice that the budget was exceeded once the tokens are already spent: step 4 took the session from 41,800 to 64,400, 14,400 tokens over the limit. How far it overshoots depends on the size of the last call, and in an agent the input grows every step because the whole transcript is sent again, so the overshoot grows too. To stay within a budget, check before the call with an upper-bound estimate: the input tokens are known before sending (count them), and the output can be bounded by the maxOutputTokens cap. The misconception is that checking often is the same as checking first.

questions.question:
Price table (example numbers, USD per million tokens = micro-USD per token): large input 3, output 15. Every call is sent with maxOutputTokens = 1000.
Session cost budget: 60,000 micro-USD; spent so far: 50,000.

The tracker checks before the next call:
estimated cost = 2,000 input tokens * 3 + 1,000 * 15 = 21,000
50,000 + 21,000 = 71,000 > 60,000  -> stop("max_cost")

The team replays the same request without the check: the model writes 200 output tokens, so the call costs 2,000 * 3 + 200 * 15 = 9,000 micro-USD (59,000 in total).

Statement: "The check refused a call that would have fit in the budget, and that is the expected cost of an estimate that guarantees the budget is never exceeded."
questions.explanation: True. The output length is unknown before the call, so a check that must never overshoot has to assume the worst case the API allows: the maxOutputTokens cap. That estimate is an upper bound, so it sometimes refuses calls that would have fit, like this one. You can reduce those refusals by lowering maxOutputTokens for steps that only need short answers, or by switching to a cheaper model near the end of a budget, but not by estimating the output from an average: an average is exceeded about half the time. The misconception is that a refused call that would have fit means the check is wrong; it means the check is conservative, which is the property you asked for.

challenges.name: agent-budget-tracker
challenges.title: Budget tracker: tokens, cost, time and tool calls
challenges.description:
One BudgetTracker serves the CodeDev support agent across many sessions. The agent loop (in the test runner) asks it before every model call and every tool call and tells it what each call used. Write the tracker.

- startSession(userId, day): a session starts at clock.now(); per-session usage starts at 0; the user's spend on that UTC day ("YYYY-MM-DD") carries over from earlier sessions.
- beforeModelCall(model, inputTokens): decide before the call, from an estimate. The output is estimated as config.maxOutputTokens (the cap: real output never exceeds it). Estimated tokens = inputTokens + maxOutputTokens; estimated cost = inputTokens * inputPerMTok + maxOutputTokens * outputPerMTok (prices are USD per million tokens = micro-USD per token, so all costs are integers). Return the first limit the call could exceed, in this order, or null: "unknown_model" (no price: fail closed), "max_tokens" (session tokens + estimate > session.maxTokens), "max_cost" (session cost + estimate > session.maxCostMicros), "daily_cost" (user's spend that day + estimate > dailyCostMicrosPerUser), "max_wall_ms" (elapsed session time + modelCallMsEstimate > session.maxWallMs). Reaching a limit exactly is allowed.
- recordModelCall(model, usage): add the actual input/output tokens and their cost to the session and to the user's daily spend.
- beforeToolCall(tool): "tool_calls:<tool>" if this call would exceed session.maxToolCalls[tool]; unlisted tools are unlimited. recordToolCall(tool) counts it.
- report(): { modelCalls, inputTokens, outputTokens, costMicros, wallMs, toolCalls (only tools called), remaining: { tokens, costMicros, wallMs, dailyCostMicros, toolCalls (every tool in maxToolCalls) } }. A remaining value never goes below 0.

Input (stdin, JSON): { "config", "sessions": [ { "id", "user", "start" (ISO, UTC), "turns": [ { "model", "input", "output", "ms", "tool"?, "toolMs"?, "final"? } ] } ] }. The fake model stops writing at maxOutputTokens; all times are on a fake clock. Output: a JSON array, one object per session: { "session", "user", "answered", "stoppedBy", ...report() }.
hints: Which of these numbers can you know before a model call, and which only after it? The tracker has to decide with the first kind and record the second kind - and some of what it records must survive startSession while the rest must not.

Look at the two kinds of state: per-session counters (reset in startSession) and the daily spend, which belongs to the pair (user, day) and must outlive sessions - a Map keyed by both works. In beforeModelCall, compute the token and cost estimate once, then test the limits in the order the description lists, each as used + estimate > limit.

A similar check on other numbers: a 10 MB upload quota with 9.2 MB used and a file whose size is only known as "at most 1 MB". 9.2 + 1 = 10.2 > 10, so refuse before uploading, even if the file turns out to be 0.5 MB. After an accepted upload, add the real size; the remaining quota shown to the user is max(0, 10 - used).

tests.name: A session that stays within every budget reports what is left
The call that could pass the token budget is not made (estimate includes max output)
Session cost: the large model is stopped before a call that could exceed the cost limit
Tool budgets per tool; tools that are not listed are unlimited
Daily budget per user carries across sessions and resets on the next UTC day
Wall time: stop when elapsed time plus the call estimate would pass the limit; check order
Invalid input: a model with no price is refused before it is called
Large: 120 sessions of 8 users over 3 days
